Probably my favourite game of all time. 

The games basic premise, functionality and gameplay takes a lot from Uplink (my favourite hacking game after this), which is not a bad thing in of itself. It borrowed ideas and expanded on them, and executed it wonderfully.

The story is great (and unlike what some reviews state, there's a few paths you can choose) and the soundtrack is absolutely phenomenal, really ramping up and creating tension where needed.

The real meat of the game comes from the workshop mods, and there are some really brilliant mods there (there was a multiplayer mode in the works a few years ago that was really promising, but it might have fizzled out).

I will say that the DLC is well worth getting, it's probably better than the main game, and expands on main game gameplay really well. There's a good few workshop mods that rely on the DLC, so just keep it in mind.

[h1] The Story is Incredible for a Hacker Game[/h1]


While HACKNET is Famously and mostly known for being the big Hacker game. It should also be told that this game has an amazing and gripping story.  So if you think on getting the game just for the programming part. Then the Programming Part won't be the only thing keeping you wide awake, eager to finish the game in one pull as the story grips you as much as the puzzles themselves do if not even more. The Story makes you feel the weight of your actions and while there is some funny here and there you'll see that the people you work for have clients that have very deep and sinister contracts for you to finish. (SPOILER) [spoiler] from modifying Death Row inmates. All the way to fumbling with ICU patients to remotley flat-line them. 
[/spoiler] But even those examples are just some of the side-quests you can do an track. you'll eventually find yourself doing quests not because you'll earn a new tool or program. But because you WANT to know what message you'll recieve from the client. What the client feels about it. Satisfaction? Sadness? Despair? Anger? That is all for you to find out.

The Ending is also a very fullfilling and satisfying sight to be head as you'll really get into it because even without the game showing faces or even saying a single word to you (except one part which i will not spoil), it will still make the story feel so lifeley and good. 

It's lightly emotional and i think that's what makes this neat programming worth it's original price.

Very cool hacker game. If you've ever wanted to be a darknet hacker, or have an interest in coding & IT, this game is probably right up your alley. Its got a great format that really immerses you in in the "hacker" idea. It then becomes a sort of murder-mystery game (think Clue), in which you have to use your hacking skills to uncover leads and get to the heart of the problem. 

The ability to use a mouse to select things definitely expedites things; if you want to, however, everything in the game (that I'm aware of) can be achieved entirely through keyboard commands. This aspect helps deliver the old-school "1980's hacker" vibe, when the world thought that a couple lines of computer code could cause armageddon. XD

All in all, this is a great game. It's well thought out, and has an incredibly entertaining and realistic (to a layman) interface. It doesn't hold your hand. It gives you helpful hints, offers help when needed, yet expects you to do most of the work (which does include remembering certain code commands). The story is compelling, and drives the game forwards, ensuring you want to continue hacking until you finally discover the truth of the "locked-room mystery," or in this case the "locked-computer mystery."
Feels a bit like work, but good if you would like to learn something new.
